body.x: Monitoring people for fall risk usually raises a privacy question, since cameras record faces and rooms, and the monitoring has to work as well at night as in daylight.

Cygbot Co., Ltd., a LiDAR sensor R&D company based in Anyang and led by CEO Hyunmin Lee, builds a fall-prevention system that does without cameras. At KES 2026, the company is showcasing its real-time AI fall-prevention LiDAR system and its ToF RGB-D Camera Module, and says it aims to explore technology partnerships, proof-of-concept (PoC) opportunities and new business collaborations.

The fall-prevention LiDAR combines time-of-flight (ToF) depth data with edge AI to analyze human movement and detect fall risk in real time without cameras. It also lets staff review the situation before and after an incident, and the company says it detects reliably day and night regardless of lighting. The ToF RGB-D Camera Module, an ultra-compact 3D vision sensor, combines ToF and RGB technologies to deliver depth data and color 3D information at the same time, which suits spatial perception, object recognition and humanoid and other robots. The module received a KES Innovation Award.

Cygbot's work rests on its own solid-state LiDAR and ToF technologies, which it uses to build compact, lightweight sensors for obstacle detection, distance measurement and spatial perception in autonomous mobile robots, service robots and humanoid robots.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
